# AI Security Institutes tracker

> Which states have an AI Security Institute (AISI), covering all 193 UN member states plus Taiwan and the EU AI Office, with funding, staff and leadership where published. Every record cites its sources. Published by Accelerate Europe; unpublished preview build; version 1.2.1-dev, data as of 25 November 2026.

## What's in the data

- Jurisdiction (`jurisdictions`): the AISI status of one of the 193 UN member states, Taiwan or the EU.
- AISI (`institutes`): a body that meets the definition below, or a named body planned or formally proposed for that role. We count a body as an AI Security Institute (AISI) if a national government or an international organisation, such as the EU, has tasked it with testing general-purpose or frontier AI models for their capabilities and risks, or has named it its AI safety institute or its AI security institute. Being a regulator, certification body or cyber security agency is not enough on its own.
- Related body (a jurisdiction's `related_bodies`): a body that could be mistaken for an AISI, such as an AI Act authority. Its record says why it does not qualify.
- Output (an AISI's `outputs`): a report, joint test, guidance, evaluation, tool or dataset credited to the AISI or a predecessor. Joint work appears under each of the involved AISIs.
- Agreement (an AISI's `agreements`): an agreement that names the AISI as a party or implementer. A company's pledge to give the AISI model access is listed too. Each is signed, announced or pledged (`state`).
- Network milestone (`dataset.network_milestones`): an event of the international network of AISIs, such as its founding or a joint testing exercise. It does not by itself show which members took part.
- Source (`sources`): a document we cite, with the passages we quote from it. Each quoted passage names the facts it supports (`supports`).
- Claim (a jurisdiction's or an AISI's `claims`): one sentence with the one quoted passage that supports it, and a code where a code fits. A state with none identified may have one development claim: an act quoted from the state's own primary sources, with its date (`act`, `date`), coded from `dataset.vocabularies.development`.

Jurisdiction and AISI IDs never change. New codes in `dataset.vocabularies` can appear in a minor version; removing or renaming one is a major version, except fields and vocabularies listed in `dataset.provisional`.

## Sources and dates

The sources behind each field are listed by ID in `citations`; an empty list means we have no quoted passage for that field. Each source has a title, its address (`url`), a copy saved in a web archive where one exists (`archive_url`) and the passages we quote from it (`excerpts`), each with an English translation when the source is in another language (`gloss`). The data date is `dataset.as_of`. To let others check an answer drawn from this data, give the data date and each source's title and address. Each jurisdiction and AISI records the date of its last full re-check (`check.last_checked`; see the freshness rule in `dataset.method`). Where `check.last_checked_basis` is historical_upper_bound, the last check was on or before that date.

## Status

A jurisdiction's status (`status`) is one of established, planned, proposed, exploring or none_identified, defined in `dataset.status_definitions`. Where recorded, the date the current status began (`status_since`) is as precise as its source (a year, a month or a day).

## Searches that found nothing

These four values mean our searches found nothing. They do not show that nothing exists.

- None identified (`none_identified`): no current qualifying government step towards an AISI.
- Not published (`not_published`): no published information for that field.
- None found (`none_found`): no matching evidence for that field, such as model access.
- None disclosed (a funding entry of `kind` none_disclosed): no published budget.

An omitted field or null means not known or not published, never zero or false. For budget and staff, Not published means that no figure was found in the sources checked; these searches are not yet logged with dates, unlike those for testing and access. Some fields give null, omission or an empty list another meaning, such as not applicable; their schema descriptions say which.

## Confidence

We rate the evidence as high, medium or low. Every jurisdiction's status has a rating (`status_confidence`), set by the status confidence rule in `dataset.method`. Funding amounts, staff counts and leadership entries have one where recorded (`confidence`); the schema defines its levels.

## Funding and staff

An AISI's funding (`funding`) and staff (`staff`) lists include every recorded figure, including historical figures and proposals, so the first or last entry is not necessarily the current one. The `display` fields pick the current figures, the ones the page shows, by ID (null when none qualifies):

- `display.budget`: the funding entry shown as the budget
- `display.comparison_funding`: the annual funding entry used to compare AISIs; its euro estimate is `eur_per_year_est`
- `display.staff`: the staff entry shown on the page
- `display.total_staff` and `display.technical_staff`: the latest total and technical staff counts

Not every amount is the AISI's own adopted budget. A figure can be another body's or a wider programme's money (`coverage`: not_institute_specific), only part of the budget (`coverage`: component) or proposed rather than adopted (`commitment`: proposed).

## Leadership and national partners

An AISI's head (`head`), the ministry-level body it reports to (`reports_to`) and the national bodies it is made up of or works with (`national_partners`) each have a state: stated, not published or not applicable (`state`). The head's name and title are in the AISI's list of named leaders, such as directors and their deputies (`people`, linked by `head.person_id`). Each partner's relation is member (a constituent of a federated AISI), works with, or planned (`relation`). Only the national cyber security agency, marked `cyber_agency`, is searched for at every AISI, so a missing partner of another kind does not mean there is none.

## Functions

An AISI's functions (`functions`) give each current (not retired) code in `dataset.vocabularies.function` once, in that order, with a value (`value`): mandate (a text assigns it), activity (a text shows work that exists, a named piece of work or programme or work reported as done, not a description of what the AISI is for, focuses on or plans to do), both, not_found (checked, no claim found) or not_coded (not yet checked against that code). The claims behind a value (`claim_ids`) list assignments in authored order, then live activity newest first (undated last, ties in authored order), then expired activity in authored order; `since` is the earliest live activity date unless any is undated, and `newest` names the first live activity claim. A function claim on a jurisdiction is about the related body its `body_id` names. The functions and their code list are provisional (`dataset.provisional`): codes may be added, split, renamed or removed in a minor version, and a retired code stays in the list with `deprecated` and `replaced_by`.

## Files

- [Full dataset](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/data/aisi.json) (`data/aisi.json`): every jurisdiction, AISI and source in one file
- [Schema](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/data/aisi.schema.json) (`data/aisi.schema.json`): what each field means
- [Data package](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/data/datapackage.json) (`data/datapackage.json`): every download, including one CSV per table, with column descriptions
- [Jurisdictions list](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/api/v1/jurisdictions.json) (`api/v1/jurisdictions.json`): each jurisdiction's ID, name, status, status date and AISI ID
- [One jurisdiction](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/api/v1/jurisdictions/GB.json) (`api/v1/jurisdictions/{id}.json`, for example `GB.json`): the ID is the two-letter ISO 3166-1 code (GB for the UK, GR for Greece) or EU. Holds the jurisdiction (`record`), its AISI where there is one (`institute.record`, otherwise `institute` is null) and the sources both cite (`sources`).
- [One AISI](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/api/v1/institutes/gb-aisi.json) (`api/v1/institutes/{id}.json`, for example `gb-aisi.json`): the ID is in the jurisdictions list. Holds the AISI and the sources it cites.
- [API index](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/api/v1/index.json) (`api/v1/index.json`): file locations, URL patterns, AISI IDs, status definitions and this text, as JSON
- [Page](https://accelerate-europe.github.io/aisi-tracker-preview/b/eedd44e773/) (`./`): the tracker page
